{"self_assessment": "Impact: My main contribution was quality assurance. I ran five close inspections of the build between 0:45 and 3:00, covering the back line, the nose join, and the doubled-up patch in the middle. Each time I checked how much of the table the push would knock over. I reported to the table that the whole run was connected and falling, so nobody spent time re-laying sound work. The final picture was a clear fish outline with the full run connected to the start, and my checks helped confirm that.

Execution: I checked the areas that carried the most risk, which were the joins where strokes met. When I looked at the doubled-up section in the middle, I confirmed it was connected and needed no patching. I then reported that clearly so the table could leave it alone. After that I kept my hands off the dominoes. With the run connected and the clock running down, I judged that extra handling risked bumps more than it would help.

Collaboration: I offered to lay the lower-tail stroke and, when Hana said she was already partway through it, I stepped back at once to avoid a collision. I then took on the check she asked for. I kept my messages short and clear, and I stayed out of other people's work areas so nothing got knocked.

Leadership: I didn't set the direction. I backed the fish idea early and kept the table focused on the goal of a connected run. I helped set the hands-off norm in the final minutes, which kept the finished fish intact until the push.", "my_share_percent": 12}
